text: Europe in 1200

The year 1200 opens a new age. In the east of the Mediterranean, the Christian lords hold only a thin strip of the coast. Jerusalem fell in 1187, and a truce keeps the peace. The Byzantine emperor rules a land that is smaller each year. In Egypt, the brothers and sons of Saladin fight for his lands. In Anatolia, the Turks of Rum fight each other. In the north, new kingdoms grow in Bulgaria and Hungary. Over the Latin lords stands the pope, who wants a new crusade.
The authorities

Innocent III became pope in January 1198, at the age of about 37. He teaches that the pope stands above every king, as the vicar of Christ. He wants to lead the Latin Church to a new crusade. Rome is one of the five great sees of the old church, with Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch and Jerusalem. Since the split of 1054 Rome and Constantinople do not share the altar. The caliph of Baghdad has a religious rank in Islam, but his power is small. The sultans hold the real power.
The sparks of the war

Four fires burn in 1200. In 1198 Innocent called a new crusade, and the knights of France and Flanders took the cross. They need ships, and only Venice has a fleet for them. In Egypt, al-Adil took power from the sons of Saladin, and his army grows with slave soldiers who are called mamluks. In Constantinople, Alexios III holds the throne that he took from his brother Isaac. In the north, Kaloyan of Bulgaria and Emeric of Hungary each look for a crown from Rome. Any one of these fires can burn the whole map.

Alexios III took the throne in 1195 when he blinded his brother Isaac II. The empire is poor, the fleet is old and the lords of the provinces do not obey. He wants to keep the throne and to stop the raids of Bulgaria. He fears his nephew Alexios, the son of Isaac, and the Latin knights. His first goal is to make peace with the Bulgarians and to build ships.

Kaloyan is the tsar of the Bulgarians and the Vlachs. His brothers won the freedom of the land from Byzantium, and they were killed. He wants a royal crown that the pope gives, and the lands of the Balkans that Byzantium holds. He fears Hungary in the north and the Byzantine army. His first goal is to write to Innocent III and to raid the Byzantine border.

Suleiman II holds Konya, the capital of the Turks of Rum. He took it in 1196 from his brother, and the brothers still fight for the lands. He wants to unite Anatolia under his rule. He fears Georgia in the east and the emperors of Constantinople in the west. His first goal is to keep his emirs loyal and to win the cities of his brothers.

Al-Adil is the brother of Saladin. In 1196 he took Damascus, and in 1200 he took Egypt from the sons of Saladin. He wants one Ayyubid state in Egypt and Syria, and a peace with the Franks. He fears the sons of Saladin and the Latin knights who will come with a new crusade. His first goal is to hold Cairo, and to pay his army of slave soldiers.

Emeric rules a strong kingdom in the middle of Europe. He took the cross in 1196 and did not go. His brother Andrew wants the throne, and the two fight in a long quarrel. Emeric wants to bring Bulgaria and Serbia under his crown. He fears his brother and the dukes of Austria. His first goal is to make peace in his house and to keep the friendship of the pope.

Leopold VI is the duke of Austria and of Styria. His house won Styria in 1192 by a treaty. He wants to keep both duchies and to make Vienna a rich city. He fears Hungary, Bohemia and the lords of Bavaria. His first goal is to make a friend of the German king and to guard the road of the Danube.

The papal state holds the land around Rome, and Innocent III wants all of it back. He wants the Holy Land freed and the kings of Europe at his feet. He fears the German captains in Italy and a king of the Germans who is too strong. His first goal is to take back the towns of the papal state and to start the crusade.

Enrico Dandolo is the doge of Venice. He is very old and almost blind, and his mind is sharp. Venice wants the trade of the east and the sea of the Adriatic. It fears Genoa and Pisa and the cities of the Dalmatian coast. Its first goal is to sell ships to the crusade, because only Venice has a fleet for it.

Frederick II is a child of five, king of Sicily since 1198. His mother Constance died in that year, and the pope is his guardian. The lords of the realm want to rule in his name. German captains such as Markward of Anweiler hold lands in the south of Italy. His first goal is to grow up and to keep the island kingdom whole.

Muhammad al-Nasir is the caliph of Marrakesh, and his army is the largest of the west. He wants the end of the Banu Ghaniya in Ifriqiya and in Majorca, and the end of the Christian kings of Spain. He fears an alliance of those kings, because the pope calls them to a crusade. His first goal is to free Ifriqiya and to gather a great army for Spain.

The Banu Ghaniya are the last family of the Almoravid lords. They hold the Balearic islands and fight in Ifriqiya, and they raid the coast from their ships. They want to hold Tunis and Bejaia and to stay out of the reach of the Almohads. They fear the army of the caliph. Their first goal is to hold the cities that they have won.

Aimery of Lusignan is the king of Jerusalem, but the holy city is in the hands of the Muslims since 1187. His court is in Acre, and his kingdom is a strip of towns along the coast. A truce with al-Adil keeps the peace. He wants Jerusalem back, and a crusade that comes with a strong army. He fears the army of Egypt. His first goal is to keep the truce and to hold the coast.

Bohemond III is an old prince, and he has ruled Antioch since 1163. His son and his grandson both want the city. He wants to keep his land and to stop Leo of Cilicia, who claims Antioch for his own family. He fears the Armenians in the north and the army of Egypt in the south. His first goal is to find a strong friend for his house.

Leo rules the mountains of Cilicia, and in 1198 he took the title of king. The pope and the German emperor sent him the crown. He wants to unite Cilicia and Antioch. He fears the Turks of Rum in the north and the Byzantines in the west. His first goal is to win the friendship of Rome and to make his claim on Antioch stronger.

The Lusignan family rules Cyprus. Richard the Lionheart took the island in 1191, and then he sold it to the Templars, who gave it back. Cyprus became a kingdom in 1197. It is a rich island, and it feeds the Latin towns of the coast. The family wants to keep the island safe and to make it a base of the crusade. It fears the Byzantine emperor, who says that the island is his. Its first goal is to build ships and to grow the towns.

Tamar is the queen of Georgia, and her reign is the golden age of the kingdom. She rules from the Black Sea to the Caspian Sea. She wants to hold the lands that she has won, and to make her neighbours pay tribute. She fears the Turks of Rum and the atabegs of Azerbaijan. Her first goal is to keep the nobles loyal and to guard her border.

Al-Nasir is the caliph of Baghdad. His family holds the first rank of Islam, but the sultans hold the power. He wants to make the caliphate strong again, and to hold Iraq. He fears the shah of Khwarazm in the east and the Seljuk lords of the plateau. His first goal is to make allies of the lords around Baghdad.
